features.feature_value: Uses presence of open cussing/profanity as the key reason for removing content.
features.evidence_span: The open cussing is how I decided what shuld be thrown out.
features.rationale: The participant explicitly ties their keep/remove decision to profanity.

features.feature_value: Focuses on whether there are curse words or very offensive statements.
features.evidence_span: if there were any curse words or very offensive statements
features.rationale: Their stated evaluation criteria centers on curse/offensiveness.

features.feature_value: Rejects content with foul language or name calling; emphasizes staying civil and avoiding hate/offensive influence for youth.
features.evidence_span: I did not approve any content that used foul language or name calling
features.rationale: They clearly state profanity/name-calling as disqualifying, with youth-appropriateness as justification.

features.feature_value: Indicates party-focused framing had little impact; prioritizes harm cues like dangerous medical advice or promoting violence.
features.evidence_span: The fact that they were both party focused really had no effect on me... harmful (known bad medical advice) or promote violence.
features.rationale: They directly compare pair influence to a harm-focused decision criterion and say party focus mattered little.

features.feature_value: Removal rationale centers on bullying and profanity while endorsing respectful discourse if civil.
features.evidence_span: I removed posts these were Bullying and Profane. I think respectful discourse is great, if it stays civil.
features.rationale: Their keep/remove explanation explicitly links bullying/profanity to removal and civility to allowance.

features.feature_value: Gives a terse language-abuse/no-discussion statement implying limited consideration beyond profanity/verbal abuse.
features.evidence_span: Swearing, verbal abuse, no issues, no discussion, no point
features.rationale: The reflection is short and primarily lists language-abuse-related cues with little elaboration about the pair.

features.feature_value: Describes the posts as very extreme without detailing pair comparison effects.
features.rationale: This provides a single general content appraisal (extreme) rather than a pair-based influence mechanism.

features.feature_value: Perceives both sides expressing disagreements/making the other the bad guy; suggests this broad partisan dynamic provides limited impact.
features.evidence_span: MOSTLY from both liberals as well as conservatives... want to make the other out to be the bad guy
features.rationale: They characterize the content as broadly partisan across both versions/sides, aligning with low perceived influence.
